items.text: Badge pages and event details show the exact UTC time next to your local time, for example Oct 15, 06:00 (04:00 UTC).
Castlevania: Belmont's Curse dates added: Oct 15, 04:00 to Nov 2, 03:59 UTC.
Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine II (Ultramarine) ends Oct 29 at 06:59 UTC.
LoL 2026 World Championship: Worlds 2026 Supporter and the Heartsteel, K/DA, Pentakill and True Damage Fan badges are one event, with the objective: sub or gift a Tier 1 sub in League of Legends.
Privacy Policy, Terms of Service and Legal Notice updated: live stream data on Watch now and Top Categories, Remind me notifications, the Discord bot, our servers and data sources.
Home page sliders: bigger cards, long badge names use two lines, and the date reads "Added today", "yesterday" or "3 days ago", so nothing breaks onto extra lines.

Remind me: get a browser notification when a badge's dates are announced, when it starts and a day before it ends (2 hours before for short events). Find the button on badge pages and in the event details.
Notification links open the right badge page or event directly.
Faster pages: the large channel badge list (about 440 KB) now loads only on the Channel Badges pages and when you search.
Returning visitors download data only when it has changed since their last visit.
A lighter logo image on the home page and an early connection to Twitch's image server, so badge images appear sooner.
The Changelog dot also lights up for new items added on the same day.
On phones, the event details panel opened under the top bar, hiding its close button.
An event panel you opened no longer closes by itself when fresh data arrives a moment later.
Watch now on badge pages: the biggest live streams where a running badge can be earned, updated every 15 minutes. Our own stream comes first when it is live in that category.
Last chance: badges that end within 48 hours, at the top of the home page.
Bottom navigation bar on phones: Home, Timeline, Badges, Search and Live.
Share button on badge pages (the share menu on phones, a post on X on desktop).
A dot next to Changelog when there is something new since your last visit.
New logo with a transparent background across the site and in the browser tab.
The header shows the full name, Badge Database, on one line.
Light, dark and system themes: pick one in the top right corner (on phones: at the bottom of the menu).
Changelog page: every update to Badge Database in one place.
Coming soon: a Badge Leaderboard for Twitch's top badge collectors (see Leaderboard in the menu).
"Log in with Twitch" moved to the top right corner (on phones: the icon next to search). When logged in, click your picture to log out.
Discord: separate channels for new badges, events that just started, badges ending soon and new global emotes, each with its own role to get pinged.
Discord: every badge event on the timeline also appears in the server's Events list, with start, end and how to get each badge.
Discord bot with /active, /soon and /badge commands.
Quick search finds Top Categories, Contact, Changelog and Legal Notice too.
Dates no longer show one day early for visitors in American time zones.
A notice on every page while our Discord server is temporarily unavailable. Discord links are paused until it is back.
Corrected dates for CrossWorlds World Championship 2026 (ended Oct 11, 03:58 UTC), Bloody Finger ELDEN RING (Oct 1, 07:00 to Oct 29, 06:59 UTC) and Rematch Blue Lock (ends Oct 21, 22:58 UTC).
Clearer objectives for Rematch Blue Lock and d20: watch 30 minutes.
The calendars show the newest badges first, upcoming ones included.
Stat tiles on the home page: Active now, Upcoming, Date TBA and Free today. Click a tile to jump to that part of the timeline.
Counts on the home page and the timeline are badge counts instead of event counts, so both always show the same numbers.
"Now available" posts on X show every badge of the event side by side and list each badge with its own objective.
"Now available" posts show the end date without a countdown.
Long badge names no longer overlap the bottom of the X post image.
Start and end dates added for DayZ Yellow King, Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen and Vaultbreakers.
When a badge event starts, @BadgeDatabase posts "Now available on Twitch" with the badge image, the objective and the end date, then replies with the link to the badge page.
Top Categories page: the 150 biggest Twitch categories right now, with viewers, live channels, the biggest stream and the badges you can earn there.
Home page: top categories, the most popular badges, and moving sliders for the badges you can get right now and the recently added ones.
Back to top button on long pages, on desktop and mobile.
Cleaner home page: "What is BadgeDB?" removed and "Get notified" moved to the bottom.
RuneFest 2026 badges (Yellow Party Hat, RuneScape Shrimp): exact start and end times and the participating channels.
Badge pages show up to 100 participating channels.
Quick search on every page (Ctrl+K, ⌘K or /): badges, events, channel badges, emotes and pages.
Statistics page: badges per month and year, free vs paid, and the games with the most badges.
Add to calendar on badge pages: Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook, with a reminder at the start and a last-chance reminder.
Contact page with a ready-to-send email form. Badge pages got a "Report a mistake" link.
Legal Notice page: operator, hosting, domain, trademarks and content removal.
A real 404 page with suggestions and search, instead of jumping back to the home page.
Better privacy: the 24/7 stream only loads when you click it, and the font is served from our own server instead of Google Fonts.
New sidebar groups (Insights, Help), and the "DB" in the logo is now purple.

title: Log in with Twitch and channel lists

items.text: Log in with Twitch (optional): see how a badge looks next to your own name and chat colour. No permissions are requested and your data stays in your browser.
Badge pages list the channels where the badge can be earned.
Badges announced before Twitch published them are linked to the real badge automatically.
Badge Popularity includes every badge with its full user count.
Free and paid labels follow the event's own objective.
Every badge has its own page, for example badgedatabase.com/badges/wolf-medallion/, and the site has a sitemap for search engines.
Global Emotes page: every global emote with the date it appeared, plus the removed ones.
Badge Popularity page: badges ranked by how many users wear them (data: PotatBotat).
Status labels and filters: Active, Ends soon, Upcoming, Date not announced and Ended.
Badge pages show the objective, the category, the start and end, and Twitch's own description.
X posts get a reply with the link to the badge page as soon as it is online.
Dates are filled in automatically from Twitch reward campaigns when Twitch has them.
Finished badges leave the timeline right away. Badges without dates count as ended 21 days after they appeared.
Full Privacy Policy and Terms of Service. Contact: support@badgedatabase.com.
"Badges available right now" calendar on the home page and the timeline, with week and 4-week views.
FAQ page.
New site icons for browser tabs and phone home screens.
Channel badges (sub, watch time and top supporter) are collected automatically from live channels.
Timeline events with dates and objectives.
Badge Database is live on badgedatabase.com: home page, timeline, global badge archive, channel badges, Privacy Policy and Terms.
Twitch's global badge list is checked every 15 minutes, and new badges are posted on X @BadgeDatabase with a generated image.
